title: W3C DTCG Standard & Token Taxonomies (CTI)
problemStatement:
The W3C Design Tokens Community Group specification, `$value` and `$type` schemas, and Category-Type-Item (CTI) naming taxonomies.

**Enterprise Importance**:
The W3C DTCG format has become the universal JSON schema standard across Figma, Tokens Studio, Style Dictionary, and enterprise tooling.
interviewTrap: Inventing proprietary ad-hoc JSON formats for tokens that cannot be ingested by modern design tools or Style Dictionary transforms.

solutionCode:
### CTI (Category, Type, Item) Taxonomy
CTI organizes tokens into a deterministic hierarchy:
1. **Category**: High-level domain (`color`, `font`, `size`, `motion`, `elevation`).
2. **Type**: Specific subset (`surface`, `text`, `border`, `icon`).
3. **Item**: The distinct component or element (`button`, `card`, `dialog`).
4. **Sub-item / State**: Variant or interactive state (`primary`, `hover`, `disabled`).

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: DTCG standardizes token representation in JSON using `$value`, `$type`, and `$description`. Combined with Category-Type-Item (CTI) structuring, tools can reliably transform tokens into CSS variables, Android XML, and iOS Swift.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Design Token Layer: Primitives, semantic aliases, and component tokens established.
2. Component Architecture: Headless state and keyboard accessibility hooks implemented.
3. Styling & Cascade: Zero-runtime CSS variables and layer specificity managed.
4. Governance & Packaging: Tree-shaking, semantic versioning, and telemetry monitored.
